core_summary: This chapter systematically groups materials based on observable physical properties including lustre, hardness, solubility, and light transparency (transparent, translucent, opaque). It formally defines Matter as anything possessing mass and occupying volume, linking material selection to functional design.
key_concepts: Distinction between Objects (tangible items) and Constituent Materials (substances used to make them).
Grouping Properties: Lustre (shiny vs dull), Hardness (compressible vs resistant), Solubility (dissolves in water vs settles/floats).
Light Transmission: Transparent (clear view), Translucent (blurred view), and Opaque (no light passes).
Definition of Matter: Anything that has mass and occupies space (volume).

key_terms.definition: Any physical entity that possesses mass and occupies physical space (volume).
The shiny or glossy surface appearance characteristic of metals.
Materials that allow light to pass through partially, making objects behind them appear blurry.

key_takeaways: Materials are selected to make objects based on their specific physical properties and utility.
Matter includes solids, liquids, and gases, all of which occupy volume and have mass.
Grouping materials simplifies the study of their properties and systematic applications.
